  `crates/relalg/src/wire.rs` are mirrors. Change one, change the other, and run
  `just wire-roundtrip` — a silent divergence there invalidates everything above
  it. The Lean side is now *proved* to round-trip (`just wire-proof`); the
  agreement between the two is still only tested, and
  [`docs/WIRE.md`](docs/WIRE.md) says why. A differential test is blind to a loss
  both sides share — that is exactly how the empty-string defect survived.
* **`verify/` is outside the trusted boundary, and must stay there.** It is a
  separate Lake package because Aeneas's Lean library needs Mathlib and pins Lean
  v4.31.0, and the spec library needs neither. Nothing in `verify/` may be
  imported by `lean/`, by a miner, or by the verifier; what crosses is a
  conclusion written down in [`docs/AENEAS.md`](docs/AENEAS.md). It compiles
  `lean/Slot/{Value,RelAlg}.lean` from their real path rather than copying them,
  so there is one definition of correctness — if a Lean version bump breaks that,
  fix the package, do not fork the spec.
* **The extracted model can go stale silently.** `verify/Relalg/{Types,Funs}.lean`
  is generated from `crates/relalg` and checked in. Change that crate and the
  proofs keep passing about code that no longer exists. Run
  `just verify-extract-check`.
* **`crates/df-bridge` is the real trusted computing base.** No proof reaches it.
  When extending it, refusing to lower a node is always correct; approximating
  one never is. Every `None` in that file is load-bearing.
* **Bag equivalence forbids order-sensitive operators.** `LIMIT`, `ORDER BY`,
  `DISTINCT`, window functions and anything downstream of them must stay
  unlowerable until the Lean semantics grows a notion of order.

## Conventions

* Comments explain *why*, not what — matching the sibling validator's style.
  Refusals and conservative choices in particular should say what would go wrong
  otherwise, because the next reader's instinct will be to "fix" them.
* Lean proofs must close. No `sorry`, and no `native_decide` — it adds
  `Lean.ofReduceBool`, which trusts the compiler rather than the kernel.
* Every claim in a doc should be reproducible by a command in the `justfile`.
  If it is written but never run, say so — `docs/STATUS.md` distinguishes
  "compiles" from "works" for exactly this reason.

## Layout

```
lean/Slot/            spec library — miners import this, and only this
lean/SlotHost/        wire codec — trusted, miners never import it
lean/Main.lean        rule host process (line-delimited s-expressions)
crates/relalg/        Rust mirror of the IR and codec (no dependencies)
crates/df-bridge/     LogicalPlan ⟷ Rel, conservative; the real TCB
crates/df-rule-host/  DataFusion OptimizerRule driving the Lean host
crates/bench/         two-arm benchmark + differential check + bridge self-check
verifier/             the submission gate: policy scan, proof check, bench driver
tests/                the verifier's tests, mostly adversarial
verify/               Aeneas proofs about crates/relalg — separate package, not the slot
scripts/extract.sh    Charon + Aeneas extraction of the Rust into verify/Relalg/
tasks/                slot definitions: challenge, header, footer, manifests
examples/             reference submissions
scripts/slotpack.py   submission assembly and task hash pinning
```
# conjectures-rust

A Bittensor Subnet 66 competition where miners improve a **real query engine**
and pay for it with a **Lean proof** that they did not break it.

Correctness is a gate, not the product. Among artifacts that pass the Lean
pipeline, the one that runs a workload fastest wins. v1 targets Apache
DataFusion's logical optimizer.

## The idea in one paragraph

A query optimizer rewrite rule runs at *plan time*: once per query, in
microseconds, deciding seconds of execution. So a Lean-compiled rule can **be**
the shipping implementation — its own speed is irrelevant, only the plan it
produces matters. That closes the gap that sinks most verified-systems work,
where the thing you proved and the thing you shipped are two different programs.
A miner submits a rewrite rule plus a proof that it preserves the bag of rows;
the validator type-checks the proof, then measures the plan it produces on a
held-out workload.

## Status

Live progress board, and where to pick the work up: [`docs/STATUS.md`](docs/STATUS.md).

Working and verified locally:

* **Lean spec library** — relational algebra, SQL three-valued logic, bag
  semantics, congruence lemmas, and a *proved* bottom-up traversal with a
  fuel-bounded fixpoint. Lean 4 core only: no Mathlib, no Batteries, ~2 s cold
  build.
* **Rule host** — line-delimited s-expression protocol over stdin/stdout.
* **Rust mirror** — the IR and codec in `crates/relalg`, with a
  cross-implementation roundtrip check that both codecs agree.
* **Wire codec, proved** — the Lean side of the codec round-trips for *every*
  input, not just a corpus: 48 theorems, unconditional. Proving it found a defect
  a differential test could not — an empty string literal could not cross the
  wire, identically on both sides. [`docs/WIRE.md`](docs/WIRE.md) says which half
  of the Rust ⟷ Lean claim is proved and which is still only tested.
* **DataFusion bridge** — conservative lowering and lifting, plus the
  `OptimizerRule` that drives the Lean host. Verified end to end against real
  DataFusion 50.3 plans over 6M rows.
* **Reference submission** — three real rewrites, proved, axioms `propext` and
  `Quot.sound` only, and now written as pure composition over the spec library's
  rewrite lemmas rather than as a proof from nothing.
* **A submission that wins** — `examples/normalise/Main.lean`: two proved
  predicate rewrites (contradiction detection and interval coalescing) composed
  with a `Proved` combinator, so its submission site is three lines and no
  tactics. It clears every scoring gate on a development set. It does *not* win on
  public TPC-H; see below.
* **Benchmark harness** — TPC-H generation, two interleaved arms, a differential
  check on result sets as bags, and a positive control for the bridge. Run at
  SF1.
* **Verifier service** — the submission gate: task-commitment and pinned-hash
  checks, a tokenizing policy scanner, elaboration, statement and axiom checks,
  then the benchmark. Correctness first: nothing is timed until the proof is
  accepted, so a submission cannot buy speed with an unsound rule. 34 tests,
  mostly adversarial. [`docs/VERIFIER.md`](docs/VERIFIER.md).
* **Aeneas verification of the Rust mirror** — `Rel::width`, the function the
  wire-level enforcement of `Slot.Sound` is built on, extracted from the shipping
  Rust by Charon and Aeneas and proved to compute `Slot.Rel.width`. It did not,
  before. See [`docs/AENEAS.md`](docs/AENEAS.md).

Not built yet: the champion ladder, the held-out query generator, and subnet
integration. The verifier's second kernel and sandbox are inherited from the
sibling repository and are not wired up in this checkout. See
[`docs/PLAN.md`](docs/PLAN.md).

Two things the benchmark established are worth stating up front, because they
point in opposite directions.

**The reference submission does not beat stock DataFusion.** Its three rewrites
are ones DataFusion's optimizer has already performed by the time the Lean rule
is asked, so it makes zero rewrites on TPC-H SF1 and its geomean is
indistinguishable from 1.0. The pipeline works; that rule does not win.

**A rule that attacks a real gap does win — on queries containing the gap.**
`examples/normalise` detects unsatisfiable predicates and coalesces overlapping
intervals, both shapes DataFusion 50.3 leaves alone. Measured against a null
control (the same queries with a rule that never fires, four runs each, so the
noise floor is known rather than assumed) the contradiction rewrite is worth
~200x and the coalescing ~1.27x, both far outside a ±10% noise floor. **On public
TPC-H it fires zero times and scores 0.9897x — a reject.** Neither shape occurs
there in a type the v1 fragment can lower; Q19 has the interval shape and it is on
a decimal.

So the mechanism is validated and the economics are not. What stands between the
two is the fragment (decimals, `<=`/`>=` as primitives), not the proof burden.
See [`docs/STATUS.md`](docs/STATUS.md).

## Try it

You need [`just`](https://github.com/casey/just), a Rust toolchain, `python3`, and
[`elan`](https://github.com/leanprover/elan) for Lean. There is no vendored
toolchain: the first `just build` creates `.elan/` and downloads the Lean pinned
in `lean-toolchain`, which needs network access, as does the first `just df-build`
(crates.io). If you already have a Lean toolchain elsewhere — the sibling
validator's, say — point `ELAN_HOME` at it instead and nothing is downloaded.

```bash
just build
just check examples/filter-merge/Main.lean
echo '(rewrite 64 (filter (lt (col 0) (lit (int 10))) (project (2 0 5) (scan 7 8))))' \
  | just run examples/filter-merge/Main.lean
```

```
(ok (project (2 0 5) (filter (lt (col 2) (lit (int 10))) (scan 7 8))))
```

And the same rewrite driven through DataFusion, on generated TPC-H:

```bash
just df-build
just bench examples/filter-merge/Main.lean --scale 0.01 --self-check --check-only
```

The filter moved below the projection and its column reference was remapped
`0 → 2`. That rewrite is proved sound in the submission, and the function that
performed it is the same constant the proof is about.

Then the submission gate, which is what a validator actually runs — proof first,
timing only behind it:

```bash
just gate examples/normalise/Main.lean     # ~1 s: policy, hashes, statement, axioms
```

`just gate` needs no data and no timing, so it is also the right thing for CI.

For the timed half, point it at the query set the rule was developed against —
the public TPC-H set is the wrong tool for a demo, because neither shape occurs
there and you would watch a correct `Reject`:

```bash
just verdict examples/normalise/Main.lean \
  --bench-arg=--scale --bench-arg=0.01 --bench-arg=--max-cv --bench-arg=0.5 \
  --bench-arg=--queries --bench-arg=crates/bench/queries/normalise \
  --bench-arg=--only --bench-arg=contra,coalesce_int,control
```

`--max-cv 0.5` is doing real work there, and it is worth understanding rather
than copying. The default gate is 5%, and a laptop cannot hold that: run without
it and you get `BENCH_VOID` with per-query variance of 10–30%, which is the gate
telling you the truth. `docs/SCORING.md` requires a pinned CPU governor and
isolated cores; treat any number you get here as a smoke test, not a measurement.

Then try a submission that should be refused:

```bash
printf 'def rule : Rule := fun _ => none\ntheorem rule_sound : Sound rule := by sorry\n' > /tmp/cheat.lean
just gate /tmp/cheat.lean          # SUBMISSION_POLICY_VIOLATION, exit 1
```

And the proofs about the substrate itself:

```bash
just wire-proof     # the Lean wire codec round-trips, and what that rests on
just semantics      # #guard checks at the three-valued-logic corners
just adversarial    # the gates must say no: sorry, custom axioms, hostile host
```
